87: A Workshop is an existing `act` node variant. Its input reports are contract `outputs` produced by
88: earlier nodes; scalar `inputs` are bound by the node. Knowledge files also appear in the contract's
89: `knowledge`. The following is an additional block within `contract.yml`, not a separate file:
90: 
91: ```yaml
92: outputs:
93:   - name: measuredInput
94:     path: flow/out/${design}/measurement.txt
95:     reader: measurement-file
96:     description: The preceding tool's measurement.
97:   - name: analysis
98:     path: research/analysis/result.txt
99:     reader: measurement-file
100:     description: The script's derived measurement, checked by the reader and Judge.
101: environment:
102:   wrappers: [sh]
103: knowledge:
104:   - file: analysis-method.md
105:     purpose: How the measurements support the analysis.
106: workshops:
107:   - id: analyze
108:     purpose: Read measuredInput and write a script deriving the requested measurement from its actual data.
109:     directory: research/analysis
110:     entry: entry.sh
111:     language: sh
112:     inputs: [LIMIT]
113:     reads: [measuredInput]
114:     knowledge: [analysis-method.md]
115:     produces: analysis
116:     argv: [sh, '${ENTRY}', '${WORKSPACE}', '${LIMIT}']
117:     licences: {}             # omit when no licensed resource is needed
118: ```
119: 
120: The corresponding graph node and downstream read are real nodes, connected after the input producer:
121: 
122: ```yaml
123: - id: analyze
124:   kind: act
125:   parameters:
126:     workshop: analyze
127:     arguments:
128:       LIMIT: { from: strategy, name: stepMs }
129: - id: read-analysis
130:   kind: act
131:   parameters:
132:     observes: analysis
133: ```
134: 
135: `reads` and `produces` are exact `contract.outputs[].name` values. The model's read tool takes that
136: same output name. `@workshop-input:<name>` is an internal diagnostic label; it is not a declared
137: output, path, or read argument. `produces` names an output, not the value type its reader emits.
138: The output's reader emits types declared by `semantics.yml`; downstream Judge rules consume those
139: types. `directory` is relative to the Campaign workspace and cannot be `flow` or the readers'
140: reserved directory. `entry` is one filename. `argv[0]` is a declared Site wrapper, and `argv[1]`
141: is exactly `${ENTRY}`. A script may produce a declared output elsewhere in the Campaign workspace;
142: its code-writing tool is confined to the admitted code directory. Neither may escape the Site permit.
143: 
144: | Operand | Meaning for a controlled execution |
145: | --- | --- |
146: | `${ENTRY}` | The generated entry script inside this execution's private code directory. |
147: | `${WORKSPACE}` | The Campaign root containing `flow/` and the declared output paths. |
148: | `${WORKSHOP}` | This execution's private code directory beneath the declared `directory`, including its execution identity. |
149: 
150: This example passes `WORKSPACE`, so shell `$1` is the Campaign root and `$2` is LIMIT. Its input
151: and output paths start from `$1`. A script needing helper files in its private code directory may
152: also need a `WORKSHOP` operand; use the approved spec's exact operand order and document each shell
153: position. Obtain the Campaign root from `WORKSPACE`, never by assuming a number of parent directories
154: above `WORKSHOP`. The example supplies file shape, not permission to replace the spec's argv.
155: 
156: Reader scripts have their own argv: below `$1` is `${REPORT}` and `$2` is `${OUT}`. These are argv
157: arrays; shell commands, pipes and redirections belong inside scripts.
158: 
159: ## `graph.yml` — the four node kinds, the outcomes the edges are taken on, and the one edge back
160: 
161: The block illustrates node and edge syntax. For an executable Explore method, supply the actual
162: constraint and Goal rules from the spec: the preceding Judge needs at least two ordered rules,
163: constraint first and Goal second. The single rule skeleton here does not supply that whole method.
164: 
165: ```yaml
166: id: example-probe            # the contract's id
167: version: '1'                 # the contract's version
168: entry: measure               # the node a campaign starts at
169: 
170: nodes:
171:   - id: measure              # act: run one of the contract's tools on the Site and wait for it
172:     kind: act
173:     parameters:
174:       tool: measure
175:       arguments:             # what the Run supplies for this generation
176:         STEP_MS: { from: strategy, name: stepMs }
177: 
178:   - id: read-measurement     # act: read one of the contract's outputs into the ledger
179:     kind: act
180:     parameters:
181:       observes: measurement
182: 
183:   - id: judge                # judge: apply rules in order; the edge out is chosen by the first one's outcome
184:     kind: judge
185:     parameters:
186:       rules: [measurement-within-bound]
187:       bind:                  # what binds each parameter a rule declares
188:         bound_ms: { from: goal, name: measurement_at_most }
189: 
190:   - id: next-step            # explore: choose the next strategy, or open a loop of its own
191:     kind: explore
192:     parameters:
193:       chooser: step-back-off # by id, exactly as a rule is named
194:       bind:                  # the numbers the chooser leaves to the pack author
195:         marginMs: 0.05
196:       converge:              # optional, and all four together: when this loop has stopped learning
197:         read: measured       # one of the chooser's own `reads`
198:         band: 0.05           # how far apart two generations must be to count as movement
199:         generations: 1       # how many successive generations must have moved by less than that
200:         generationLimit: 6   # what this pack thinks a campaign of it should be allowed at most
201: 
202:   - id: blocked              # wait: where a run stops for a person once its retries are spent
203:     kind: wait
204:     parameters:
205:       blocker: hard-blocker
206: 
207: edges:
208:   - { from: measure, to: read-measurement }            # an act node's one unlabelled edge out
209:   - { from: read-measurement, to: judge }
210:   - { from: judge, to: next-step, outcome: PASS }      # a judge node's edges carry their outcome
211:   - { from: judge, to: next-step, outcome: FAIL }
212:   - { from: next-step, to: measure, revisit: true }    # the loop: the only edge that goes back
213: ```
214: 
215: Read actual edges to audit endings. Judge routing uses the first rule's outcome, while an Explore
216: owner decision uses the current required Judge evidence. A goal-met decision ends the Run before a
217: revisit; a next-strategy decision follows the revisit only if the original generation budget allows
218: it. A terminal Judge PASS alone supplies no Campaign goal-met decision. Waits remain legitimate
219: where the approved spec calls for human clearance; compare each actual outcome path with that spec.
220: Comments such as "PASS is terminal" cannot override a PASS edge whose destination is a wait node.
221: 
222: ## `semantics.yml` — what the value types this pack's own readers emit mean
223: 
224: Written **only** where this pack's own readers emit a value type. A pack whose outputs are all read
225: by readers the harness ships declares none and writes no such file.
226: 
227: The two qualifier vocabularies are the harness's own and are **fixed**: `mode` is `setup` or `hold`,
228: `scope` is `all` or `reg2reg`. Declaring either means every reading of that type carries one of the
229: listed words; declaring neither means a reading of it carries no qualifier at all.
230: 
231: ```yaml
232: values:
233:   measured_ms:               # the slug a reader emits and a rule or chooser reads
234:     unit: ms                 # what a value of it is measured in; every reading is held to this
235:     mode: [setup, hold]      # optional: the analysis passes a value of it can belong to
236:     scope: [all, reg2reg]    # optional: the path groups a value of it can cover
237:     description: what this generation measured, as the file states it
238: ```
239: 
240: ## `rules/<id>.yml` — one judge rule
241: 
242: ```yaml
243: id: measurement-within-bound # the file's own name, without the .yml
244: version: '1'
245: title: The measurement is within the bound the run was started with
246: parameter:                   # optional: the one value a node binds at judge time
247:   name: bound_ms
248:   unit: ms
249: requires:                    # what must have been observed for this rule to have an opinion at all
250:   - type: measured_ms
251: subject:                     # the value the predicate is about
252:   type: measured_ms
253: predicate:
254:   op: lte                    # lte, gte and the like
255:   threshold: { parameter: bound_ms }   # or a number written here
256:   unit: ms
257: ```
258: 
259: ## `choosers/<id>.yml` — one explore move, as data
260: 
261: ```yaml
262: id: step-back-off
263: version: '1'
264: title: Take the step back by what the last generation missed by
265: parameter:                   # the one number the pack binds in its explore node's `bind:`
266:   name: marginMs
267:   unit: ms
268: reads:                       # what is read out of the run's latest observation, by type
269:   measured: { type: measured_ms, unit: ms }
270: decide:                      # first matching clause wins
271:   - when: { constraint: PASS, goal: PASS }
272:     goalMet: true            # the goal is reached; there is no next strategy
273:   - when: { constraint: PASS }
274:     next:                    # sets this pack's own strategy knobs by name; a knob not named carries over
275:       stepMs: { sum: [measured, marginMs] }
276:   - when: { constraint: FAIL }
277:     next:
278:       stepMs: { sum: [measured, { neg: marginMs }] }
279: ```
280: 
281: ## `readers/<id>.yml` and its script under `tools/` — a reader of this pack's own
282: 
283: ```yaml
284: id: measurement-file
285: version: '1'
286: file: tools/read-measurement.sh   # under this folder's tools/, and a plain file
287: argv:                             # every word is a literal, or exactly one of the four placeholders
288:   - sh                            # argv[0] is the wrapper: a literal word the contract declares
289:   - ${READER}                     # the script's path on the Site
290:   - ${REPORT}                     # the output the contract pointed it at
291:   - ${OUT}                        # the file the script must write
292: reportKind: example-measurement   # a word for the record; never sniffed
293: emits: [measured_ms]              # every value type it writes, each declared in the semantics
294: ```
295: 
296: Its script, under this folder's `tools/`, launched by the harness as a job under the Site's permit
297: with the report and the output file as arguments:
298: 
299: ```sh
300: #!/bin/sh
301: # tools/read-measurement.sh — reads $1 (the report) and writes the reading document to $2.
302: set -eu
303: printf '{"values":[{"type":"measured_ms","unit":"ms","mode":"setup","scope":"all","value":%s}]}\n' \
304:   "$(awk '/^measured/ { print $2 }' "$1")" > "$2"
305: ```
306: 
307: What it writes to `${OUT}` — one JSON document, and exit 0:
308: 
309: ```json
310: { "values": [ { "type": "measured_ms", "unit": "ms", "mode": "setup", "scope": "all", "value": 2.5 } ] }
311: ```
312: 
313: A value carries `mode` and `scope` exactly when the semantics above declare them for its type, and
314: the word it carries is one of the declared ones. It may also carry `group` (the tool's own name for
315: the path group the number came from) and, where the report did not state the number at all,
316: `"value": null` with `unknownReason` saying why — never a zero standing in for a number nobody read.
317: A value whose type, unit or qualifiers are not the declared ones is refused, and the reading never
318: becomes an observation.
319: 
320: ## `knowledge/<file>.md` — one piece of this pack's domain knowledge
321: 
322: A plain Markdown file, one per entry of the contract's `knowledge:`, written for the purpose that
323: entry gives it. It guides the executing Agent; it does not establish measured facts. Explain the
324: method symbolically. Include a worked numeric result only with the exact input and parameters and
325: an observed calculation or checked result that produced it; otherwise leave the result unverified.
326: An example value copied from another dataset cannot serve as this dataset's expected answer.
327: 
328: ```markdown
329: # Why this pack changes the step the way it does
330: 
331: <the reasoning, in the author's own words, for the purpose the contract declares>
332: ```
333: 
334: ## The five records the pipeline writes
335: 
336: Each is written by one stage, and each is what carries the folder one rung further up. They are the
337: authoring account and not the pack — no campaign reads one — and the digest of the files a campaign
338: runs is taken without them.
339: 
340: | File | Written by | Sections, in this order |
341: | --- | --- | --- |
342: | `INTENT.md` | `/hima-grill` | `Business`, `Golden Flow`, `Answers`, `Ambiguities resolved`, `Knowledge applied` |
343: | `SPEC.md` | `/hima-spec` | `Goal template`, `Constraints`, `Run contract`, `Semantics`, `Judge rules`, `Choosers`, `Endings`, `Workshops`, `Knowledge` |
344: | `FABRIC.md` | `/hima-fabric` | `Files written`, `Gaps`, `Reviews` |
345: | `TEST.md` | `/hima-test` | `Site`, `Run`, `Ending`, `Generations`, `Code`, `Refusals`, `Disagreements` |
346: | `VERSION.yml` | `/hima-release`, through the harness's own verb | `pack`, `version`, `released`, `test: { record, run }`, `files:` — one sha256 per file |
347: 
348: A record validates when its ordered `##` headings are **exactly** those sections: nothing missing,
349: nothing extra, nothing twice, nothing out of order, nothing empty. `VERSION.yml` is the one of the
350: five nobody writes by hand: every hash in it is computed by the harness over the bytes in the folder.

(End of file - total 350 lines)
</content>

lines.text: # What a pack folder holds, file by file
The skeleton the fabric stage compiles to. Every block below is the **smallest file of its kind that
this harness accepts**, with one note per field saying what that field is for. Nothing here is a
method: the ids, the paths, the units and the numbers are stand-ins, and what they should be for the
pack you are writing is the spec's to say and never this file's.
Read this for shape. Read the pack installed beside the folder you are authoring for a whole example
of the first two, written by hand for a real business. Ask `hima_pack_check` whether what you wrote
is a pack: it names every fault in the pack's own files, and that answer is the authority no
skeleton can be.
A pack folder holds, at its top: `contract.yml`, `graph.yml`, `semantics.yml` where the pack's own
readers emit value types, and the directories `rules/`, `choosers/`, `readers/`, `knowledge/` and
`tools/` where it has files for them. Every path in it is a plain file with a plain name — no link,
no hidden name, nothing but letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores in each segment.
## `contract.yml` — what a Site must bind, what a generation produces, what the pack runs
```yaml
id: example-probe            # the folder's own name; lowercase letters, digits and dashes
version: '1'                 # a string, and graph.yml states the same one
title: Example probe         # what a person reads the pack under
inputs:                      # what a Site binds in its own site file; the pack binds none of them
- name: flowRoot
description: The Golden Flow's root on the Site. Read where it lies, never written.
- name: design
description: What the flow is run over, spelled as the flow's own manifests spell it.
- name: workspaceRoot
description: Where campaign workspaces are made; the Site's permit must allow writes under it.
outputs:                     # what a generation leaves in its own workspace
- name: measurement
path: flow/out/${design}/measurement.txt   # relative to the workspace; ${…} is an input above
reader: measurement-file                    # the reader that turns it into typed values
description: What this generation measured. The judged file.
- name: toolLog
path: flow/logs/${design}/tool.log         # no reader: a file a person reads after a failure
description: What the tool said while it ran.
environment:
wrappers:                  # the first word of every command line below — a tool's argv[0] and a
- make                   #   reader's; the Site's permit decides each, and a word not here is
- sh                     #   refused before a campaign starts
workspace:
copy:                      # what is copied out of flowRoot into <workspace>/flow/, once per campaign
- Makefile
- tools
- inputs/${design}
tools:
- id: measure
file: tools/measure.sh   # the script a person can run by hand, under this folder's tools/
description: One generation of the flow's own measuring stage, in the campaign's copy of it.
inputs: [WORKSPACE, DESIGN, STEP_MS]   # the variables the script reads, and the only names argv may use
licences:                # optional: what a job of this tool holds on the Site while it runs
measuring-seat: 1      # the Site declares how many it has; a tool that holds none writes no block
argv:                    # what the harness launches; argv[0] is the wrapper above
- make
- ${WORKSPACE}/flow
- DESIGN=${DESIGN}
- measure
- STEP_MS=${STEP_MS}
rules:                       # the judge rules this pack may apply, by id: this folder's rules/ first,
- measurement-within-bound #   the bundle's second
knowledge:                   # optional: this pack's own domain knowledge, one entry per file
- file: the-step-method.md
purpose: why this pack changes the step the way it does
strategy:                    # what a run is set to for one generation; at least one knob, each whole
stepMs: { type: number, unit: ms, min: 0.5, max: 10, default: 2 }
shape: { type: choice, options: [plain, dense], default: plain }
words:                       # what a person reads each number under: one entry per goal parameter the
measurement_at_most: { label: measurement at most, unit: ms }   # graph binds, one per knob above
stepMs: { label: step, unit: ms }
shape: { label: shape }    # a choice states no unit: a choice is measured in nothing
## Workshop declaration and graph binding
A Workshop is an existing `act` node variant. Its input reports are contract `outputs` produced by
earlier nodes; scalar `inputs` are bound by the node. Knowledge files also appear in the contract's
`knowledge`. The following is an additional block within `contract.yml`, not a separate file:
```yaml
outputs:
- name: measuredInput
path: flow/out/${design}/measurement.txt
reader: measurement-file
description: The preceding tool's measurement.
- name: analysis
path: research/analysis/result.txt
reader: measurement-file
description: The script's derived measurement, checked by the reader and Judge.
environment:
wrappers: [sh]
knowledge:
- file: analysis-method.md
purpose: How the measurements support the analysis.
workshops:
- id: analyze
purpose: Read measuredInput and write a script deriving the requested measurement from its actual data.
directory: research/analysis
entry: entry.sh
language: sh
inputs: [LIMIT]
reads: [measuredInput]
knowledge: [analysis-method.md]
produces: analysis
argv: [sh, '${ENTRY}', '${WORKSPACE}', '${LIMIT}']
licences: {}             # omit when no licensed resource is needed
The corresponding graph node and downstream read are real nodes, connected after the input producer:
```yaml
- id: analyze
kind: act
parameters:
workshop: analyze
arguments:
LIMIT: { from: strategy, name: stepMs }
- id: read-analysis
kind: act
parameters:
observes: analysis
`reads` and `produces` are exact `contract.outputs[].name` values. The model's read tool takes that
same output name. `@workshop-input:<name>` is an internal diagnostic label; it is not a declared
output, path, or read argument. `produces` names an output, not the value type its reader emits.
The output's reader emits types declared by `semantics.yml`; downstream Judge rules consume those
types. `directory` is relative to the Campaign workspace and cannot be `flow` or the readers'
reserved directory. `entry` is one filename. `argv[0]` is a declared Site wrapper, and `argv[1]`
is exactly `${ENTRY}`. A script may produce a declared output elsewhere in the Campaign workspace;
its code-writing tool is confined to the admitted code directory. Neither may escape the Site permit.
| Operand | Meaning for a controlled execution |
| `${ENTRY}` | The generated entry script inside this execution's private code directory. |
| `${WORKSPACE}` | The Campaign root containing `flow/` and the declared output paths. |
| `${WORKSHOP}` | This execution's private code directory beneath the declared `directory`, including its execution identity. |
This example passes `WORKSPACE`, so shell `$1` is the Campaign root and `$2` is LIMIT. Its input
and output paths start from `$1`. A script needing helper files in its private code directory may
also need a `WORKSHOP` operand; use the approved spec's exact operand order and document each shell
position. Obtain the Campaign root from `WORKSPACE`, never by assuming a number of parent directories
above `WORKSHOP`. The example supplies file shape, not permission to replace the spec's argv.
Reader scripts have their own argv: below `$1` is `${REPORT}` and `$2` is `${OUT}`. These are argv
arrays; shell commands, pipes and redirections belong inside scripts.
## `graph.yml` — the four node kinds, the outcomes the edges are taken on, and the one edge back
The block illustrates node and edge syntax. For an executable Explore method, supply the actual
constraint and Goal rules from the spec: the preceding Judge needs at least two ordered rules,
constraint first and Goal second. The single rule skeleton here does not supply that whole method.
```yaml
id: example-probe            # the contract's id
version: '1'                 # the contract's version
entry: measure               # the node a campaign starts at
nodes:
- id: measure              # act: run one of the contract's tools on the Site and wait for it
kind: act
parameters:
tool: measure
arguments:             # what the Run supplies for this generation
STEP_MS: { from: strategy, name: stepMs }
- id: read-measurement     # act: read one of the contract's outputs into the ledger
kind: act
parameters:
observes: measurement
- id: judge                # judge: apply rules in order; the edge out is chosen by the first one's outcome
kind: judge
parameters:
rules: [measurement-within-bound]
bind:                  # what binds each parameter a rule declares
bound_ms: { from: goal, name: measurement_at_most }
- id: next-step            # explore: choose the next strategy, or open a loop of its own
kind: explore
parameters:
chooser: step-back-off # by id, exactly as a rule is named
bind:                  # the numbers the chooser leaves to the pack author
marginMs: 0.05
converge:              # optional, and all four together: when this loop has stopped learning
read: measured       # one of the chooser's own `reads`
band: 0.05           # how far apart two generations must be to count as movement
generations: 1       # how many successive generations must have moved by less than that
generationLimit: 6   # what this pack thinks a campaign of it should be allowed at most
- id: blocked              # wait: where a run stops for a person once its retries are spent
kind: wait
parameters:
blocker: hard-blocker
edges:
- { from: measure, to: read-measurement }            # an act node's one unlabelled edge out
- { from: read-measurement, to: judge }
- { from: judge, to: next-step, outcome: PASS }      # a judge node's edges carry their outcome
- { from: judge, to: next-step, outcome: FAIL }
- { from: next-step, to: measure, revisit: true }    # the loop: the only edge that goes back
Read actual edges to audit endings. Judge routing uses the first rule's outcome, while an Explore
owner decision uses the current required Judge evidence. A goal-met decision ends the Run before a
revisit; a next-strategy decision follows the revisit only if the original generation budget allows
it. A terminal Judge PASS alone supplies no Campaign goal-met decision. Waits remain legitimate
where the approved spec calls for human clearance; compare each actual outcome path with that spec.
Comments such as "PASS is terminal" cannot override a PASS edge whose destination is a wait node.
## `semantics.yml` — what the value types this pack's own readers emit mean
Written **only** where this pack's own readers emit a value type. A pack whose outputs are all read
by readers the harness ships declares none and writes no such file.
The two qualifier vocabularies are the harness's own and are **fixed**: `mode` is `setup` or `hold`,
`scope` is `all` or `reg2reg`. Declaring either means every reading of that type carries one of the
listed words; declaring neither means a reading of it carries no qualifier at all.
```yaml
values:
measured_ms:               # the slug a reader emits and a rule or chooser reads
unit: ms                 # what a value of it is measured in; every reading is held to this
mode: [setup, hold]      # optional: the analysis passes a value of it can belong to
scope: [all, reg2reg]    # optional: the path groups a value of it can cover
description: what this generation measured, as the file states it
## `rules/<id>.yml` — one judge rule
```yaml
id: measurement-within-bound # the file's own name, without the .yml
version: '1'
title: The measurement is within the bound the run was started with
parameter:                   # optional: the one value a node binds at judge time
name: bound_ms
unit: ms
requires:                    # what must have been observed for this rule to have an opinion at all
- type: measured_ms
subject:                     # the value the predicate is about
type: measured_ms
predicate:
op: lte                    # lte, gte and the like
threshold: { parameter: bound_ms }   # or a number written here
unit: ms
## `choosers/<id>.yml` — one explore move, as data
```yaml
id: step-back-off
version: '1'
title: Take the step back by what the last generation missed by
parameter:                   # the one number the pack binds in its explore node's `bind:`
name: marginMs
unit: ms
reads:                       # what is read out of the run's latest observation, by type
measured: { type: measured_ms, unit: ms }
decide:                      # first matching clause wins
- when: { constraint: PASS, goal: PASS }
goalMet: true            # the goal is reached; there is no next strategy
- when: { constraint: PASS }
next:                    # sets this pack's own strategy knobs by name; a knob not named carries over
stepMs: { sum: [measured, marginMs] }
- when: { constraint: FAIL }
next:
stepMs: { sum: [measured, { neg: marginMs }] }
## `readers/<id>.yml` and its script under `tools/` — a reader of this pack's own
```yaml
id: measurement-file
version: '1'
file: tools/read-measurement.sh   # under this folder's tools/, and a plain file
argv:                             # every word is a literal, or exactly one of the four placeholders
- sh                            # argv[0] is the wrapper: a literal word the contract declares
- ${READER}                     # the script's path on the Site
- ${REPORT}                     # the output the contract pointed it at
- ${OUT}                        # the file the script must write
reportKind: example-measurement   # a word for the record; never sniffed
emits: [measured_ms]              # every value type it writes, each declared in the semantics
Its script, under this folder's `tools/`, launched by the harness as a job under the Site's permit
with the report and the output file as arguments:
```sh
#!/bin/sh
# tools/read-measurement.sh — reads $1 (the report) and writes the reading document to $2.
set -eu
printf '{"values":[{"type":"measured_ms","unit":"ms","mode":"setup","scope":"all","value":%s}]}\n' \
"$(awk '/^measured/ { print $2 }' "$1")" > "$2"
What it writes to `${OUT}` — one JSON document, and exit 0:
```json
{ "values": [ { "type": "measured_ms", "unit": "ms", "mode": "setup", "scope": "all", "value": 2.5 } ] }
A value carries `mode` and `scope` exactly when the semantics above declare them for its type, and
the word it carries is one of the declared ones. It may also carry `group` (the tool's own name for

# What a pack folder holds, file by file
The skeleton the fabric stage compiles to. Every block below is the **smallest file of its kind that
this harness accepts**, with one note per field saying what that field is for. Nothing here is a
method: the ids, the paths, the units and the numbers are stand-ins, and what they should be for the
pack you are writing is the spec's to say and never this file's.
Read this for shape. Read the pack installed beside the folder you are authoring for a whole example
of the first two, written by hand for a real business. Ask `hima_pack_check` whether what you wrote
is a pack: it names every fault in the pack's own files, and that answer is the authority no
skeleton can be.

readers emit value types, and the directories `rules/`, `choosers/`, `readers/`, `knowledge/` and

no hidden name, nothing but letters, digits, dots, dashes and underscores in each segment.
## `contract.yml` — what a Site must bind, what a generation produces, what the pack runs
```yaml

version: '1'                 # a string, and graph.yml states the same one
title: Example probe         # what a person reads the pack under
inputs:                      # what a Site binds in its own site file; the pack binds none of them

description: The Golden Flow's root on the Site. Read where it lies, never written.
- name: design
description: What the flow is run over, spelled as the flow's own manifests spell it.
- name: workspaceRoot
description: Where campaign workspaces are made; the Site's permit must allow writes under it.
outputs:                     # what a generation leaves in its own workspace

wrappers:                  # the first word of every command line below — a tool's argv[0] and a

- sh                     #   refused before a campaign starts
workspace:
copy:                      # what is copied out of flowRoot into <workspace>/flow/, once per campaign
- Makefile
- tools
- inputs/${design}
tools:
- id: measure
file: tools/measure.sh   # the script a person can run by hand, under this folder's tools/
description: One generation of the flow's own measuring stage, in the campaign's copy of it.
inputs: [WORKSPACE, DESIGN, STEP_MS]   # the variables the script reads, and the only names argv may use
licences:                # optional: what a job of this tool holds on the Site while it runs
measuring-seat: 1      # the Site declares how many it has; a tool that holds none writes no block
argv:                    # what the harness launches; argv[0] is the wrapper above
- make
- ${WORKSPACE}/flow
- DESIGN=${DESIGN}
- measure
- STEP_MS=${STEP_MS}
rules:                       # the judge rules this pack may apply, by id: this folder's rules/ first,
- measurement-within-bound #   the bundle's second
knowledge:                   # optional: this pack's own domain knowledge, one entry per file
- file: the-step-method.md
purpose: why this pack changes the step the way it does
strategy:                    # what a run is set to for one generation; at least one knob, each whole
stepMs: { type: number, unit: ms, min: 0.5, max: 10, default: 2 }
shape: { type: choice, options: [plain, dense], default: plain }
words:                       # what a person reads each number under: one entry per goal parameter the
measurement_at_most: { label: measurement at most, unit: ms }   # graph binds, one per knob above
stepMs: { label: step, unit: ms }
shape: { label: shape }    # a choice states no unit: a choice is measured in nothing
## Workshop declaration and graph binding
A Workshop is an existing `act` node variant. Its input reports are contract `outputs` produced by
earlier nodes; scalar `inputs` are bound by the node. Knowledge files also appear in the contract's
`knowledge`. The following is an additional block within `contract.yml`, not a separate file:
```yaml
outputs:
- name: measuredInput
path: flow/out/${design}/measurement.txt
reader: measurement-file
description: The preceding tool's measurement.
- name: analysis
path: research/analysis/result.txt
reader: measurement-file
description: The script's derived measurement, checked by the reader and Judge.
environment:
wrappers: [sh]
knowledge:
- file: analysis-method.md
purpose: How the measurements support the analysis.
workshops:
- id: analyze
purpose: Read measuredInput and write a script deriving the requested measurement from its actual data.
directory: research/analysis
entry: entry.sh
language: sh
inputs: [LIMIT]
reads: [measuredInput]
knowledge: [analysis-method.md]
produces: analysis
argv: [sh, '${ENTRY}', '${WORKSPACE}', '${LIMIT}']
licences: {}             # omit when no licensed resource is needed
The corresponding graph node and downstream read are real nodes, connected after the input producer:
```yaml
- id: analyze
kind: act
parameters:
workshop: analyze
arguments:
LIMIT: { from: strategy, name: stepMs }
- id: read-analysis
kind: act
parameters:
observes: analysis

same output name. `@workshop-input:<name>` is an internal diagnostic label; it is not a declared
output, path, or read argument. `produces` names an output, not the value type its reader emits.
The output's reader emits types declared by `semantics.yml`; downstream Judge rules consume those
types. `directory` is relative to the Campaign workspace and cannot be `flow` or the readers'
reserved directory. `entry` is one filename. `argv[0]` is a declared Site wrapper, and `argv[1]`
is exactly `${ENTRY}`. A script may produce a declared output elsewhere in the Campaign workspace;
its code-writing tool is confined to the admitted code directory. Neither may escape the Site permit.
| Operand | Meaning for a controlled execution |
| `${ENTRY}` | The generated entry script inside this execution's private code directory. |
| `${WORKSPACE}` | The Campaign root containing `flow/` and the declared output paths. |
| `${WORKSHOP}` | This execution's private code directory beneath the declared `directory`, including its execution identity. |
This example passes `WORKSPACE`, so shell `$1` is the Campaign root and `$2` is LIMIT. Its input
and output paths start from `$1`. A script needing helper files in its private code directory may
also need a `WORKSHOP` operand; use the approved spec's exact operand order and document each shell
position. Obtain the Campaign root from `WORKSPACE`, never by assuming a number of parent directories
above `WORKSHOP`. The example supplies file shape, not permission to replace the spec's argv.
Reader scripts have their own argv: below `$1` is `${REPORT}` and `$2` is `${OUT}`. These are argv
arrays; shell commands, pipes and redirections belong inside scripts.

constraint and Goal rules from the spec: the preceding Judge needs at least two ordered rules,
constraint first and Goal second. The single rule skeleton here does not supply that whole method.
```yaml
id: example-probe            # the contract's id
version: '1'                 # the contract's version
entry: measure               # the node a campaign starts at
nodes:
- id: measure              # act: run one of the contract's tools on the Site and wait for it
kind: act
parameters:
tool: measure
arguments:             # what the Run supplies for this generation
STEP_MS: { from: strategy, name: stepMs }
- id: read-measurement     # act: read one of the contract's outputs into the ledger
kind: act
parameters:
observes: measurement
- id: judge                # judge: apply rules in order; the edge out is chosen by the first one's outcome
kind: judge
parameters:
rules: [measurement-within-bound]
bind:                  # what binds each parameter a rule declares
bound_ms: { from: goal, name: measurement_at_most }
- id: next-step            # explore: choose the next strategy, or open a loop of its own
kind: explore
parameters:
chooser: step-back-off # by id, exactly as a rule is named
bind:                  # the numbers the chooser leaves to the pack author
marginMs: 0.05
converge:              # optional, and all four together: when this loop has stopped learning
read: measured       # one of the chooser's own `reads`

generations: 1       # how many successive generations must have moved by less than that
generationLimit: 6   # what this pack thinks a campaign of it should be allowed at most

kind: wait
parameters:
blocker: hard-blocker
edges:
- { from: measure, to: read-measurement }            # an act node's one unlabelled edge out
- { from: read-measurement, to: judge }
- { from: judge, to: next-step, outcome: PASS }      # a judge node's edges carry their outcome
- { from: judge, to: next-step, outcome: FAIL }
- { from: next-step, to: measure, revisit: true }    # the loop: the only edge that goes back

owner decision uses the current required Judge evidence. A goal-met decision ends the Run before a
revisit; a next-strategy decision follows the revisit only if the original generation budget allows

where the approved spec calls for human clearance; compare each actual outcome path with that spec.

# The run contract of the library-authoring-qualification Pack: what Site `local` must bind before
# this Pack can run, what one generation leaves in its Campaign workspace, and what the Pack runs.
# The scope is deliberately local and non-commercial. It loads no Liberty file, invokes no QuaLib,
# calls no `edarun`, reads no production Library fact, requalifies no E1--E4 method and touches no
# customer data.
id: library-authoring-qualification
version: '1'
title: Library authoring-qualification check

# What a Site binds, in its own site file under `bindings:`. The same Pack runs on another Site by
# editing that file, never this one.
inputs:
  - name: flowRoot
    description: >-
      The Golden Flow's root on the Site: the local authoring-qualification flow directory holding
      analyze-library-contract.sh, read-library-contract.py and library-input.json. Read-only to a
      Campaign — a generation runs in its own copy of it, never here.
  - name: workspaceRoot
    description: >-
      Where Campaign workspaces are created. The Site's Permit must allow writes under it; nothing
      this Pack does writes anywhere else.

# What a generation leaves in its Campaign workspace. Paths are relative to the workspace.
outputs:
  - name: libraryContract
    path: library-contract/library-insight.json
    reader: library-contract-reader
    description: >-
      The whitelisted envelope one generation's validator wrote — schema, qualification,
      sourceSha256, provenance and unknowns — and the judged artifact. It is read into the single
      typed value library_contract_ready. It is not a Liberty file, a QuaLib report or a production
      Library fact.

# What the Site must let this Pack run: the first word of every command line below. The Permit's
# `allowedWrappers` decides each one.
environment:
  wrappers:
    - sh
    - python3

# How a Campaign workspace is prepared from the bound flow root, once per Campaign. The copy lands in
# `<workspace>/flow/`.
workspace:
  copy:
    - analyze-library-contract.sh
    - read-library-contract.py
    - library-input.json
    - README.md

# The Pack's one tool. A person can run `tools/library-contract-check.sh` by hand and get exactly the
# command line below; no licence seat is held, because the flow needs none.
tools:
  - id: library-contract-check
    file: tools/library-contract-check.sh
    description: >-
      One generation of the Golden Flow's own validator, run inside the Campaign's own copy of the
      flow: the five-field gate over the one handed-off input. The flow's command line is unchanged;
      the only thing this Pack adds around it is creating the declared output's directory.
    inputs: [WORKSPACE]
    argv:
      - sh
      - -c
      - 'mkdir -p "$(dirname "$2")" && exec sh "$1" "$3" "$2"'
      - library-contract-check
      - ${WORKSPACE}/flow/analyze-library-contract.sh
      - ${WORKSPACE}/library-contract/library-insight.json
      - ${WORKSPACE}/flow/library-input.json

# Every rule this Pack's judge node may apply, by reference: this folder's rules/ first.
rules:
  - library-contract-nonnegative
  - library-contract-goal

# This Pack's own domain knowledge, one entry per file under knowledge/.
knowledge:
  - file: library-contract-fields.md
    purpose: >-
      the five checked fields and their required shapes, the envelope's `schema` key, and the rule
      that an absent reading is never a zero
  - file: scope-boundary.md
    purpose: >-
      what this Pack's local TEST does and does not claim, in the words a person reads beside an
      ending

# The one number a Campaign binds at start. This Pack accepts exactly 1 count: the one handed-off
# input carries one identity, no knob varies it, and a different target is a new campaign.
goal:
  library_contract_target: { type: number, unit: count, min: 1, max: 1, default: 1 }

# What this Pack's number is called on the faces a person reads.
words:
  library_contract_target: { label: validated authoring-qualification contract, unit: count }

args.content:
# The library-authoring-qualification Pack as a HimaFabric graph: run the Golden Flow's own validator
# once, read the envelope it produced into one typed value, judge it with the constraint rule and then
# the goal rule, and let an explicit Explore decision end the Run only on PASS/PASS.
#
# There is no revisit edge and no loop. A generation varies nothing, so there is no next strategy to
# choose and no second generation to open. Four node kinds and no more: act, judge, explore, wait.
id: library-authoring-qualification
version: '1'
entry: check-contract

nodes:
  # Act: run the Pack's one tool on the Site, in the Campaign workspace, and wait for it.
  - id: check-contract
    kind: act
    parameters:
      tool: library-contract-check

  # Act: read the envelope that generation produced into HimaLedger, through the contract's own
  # reader. This is the flow's own reader, run from the Campaign's copy of the flow.
  - id: read-contract
    kind: act
    parameters:
      observes: libraryContract

  # Judge: the constraint rule first, then the goal rule whose target the Run's goal binds. The
  # outgoing edge is chosen by the outcome of the first rule listed. An absent or refused reading
  # leaves the constraint rule with no opinion, which reaches the same wait node the FAIL edge does.
  - id: judge
    kind: judge
    parameters:
      rules:
        - library-contract-nonnegative
        - library-contract-goal
      bind:
        library_contract_target: { from: goal, name: library_contract_target }

  # Explore: the only decision this Pack can take. One clause — PASS/PASS records goalMet — because a
  # generation reaches this node only through the constraint rule's PASS, and with the bound goal at
  # 1 count a present reading is also the goal rule's PASS. No generation limit is declared here: no
  # revisit edge exists for it to stop.
  - id: decide
    kind: explore
    parameters:
      chooser: library-contract-decide

  # Wait: where a Run stops for a person. The judge's FAIL edge draws here, an UNDETERMINED reading
  # is routed here by the fabric itself, and a spent Retry allowance on the act node arrives here too.
  - id: blocked
    kind: wait
    parameters:
      blocker: hard-blocker

edges:
  - { from: check-contract, to: read-contract }
  - { from: read-contract, to: judge }
  - { from: judge, to: decide, outcome: PASS }
  - { from: judge, to: blocked, outcome: FAIL }
  - { from: judge, to: blocked, outcome: UNDETERMINED }

#!/bin/sh
# tools/library-contract-check.sh — the `library-contract-check` tool of the
# library-authoring-qualification Pack: one generation of the Golden Flow's own validator.
#
# The command line below is the one contract.yml declares for this tool, so a person can reproduce a
# generation by hand exactly as HimaFabric runs it:
#
#   WORKSPACE=<workspaceRoot>/<campaign> \
#   sh packs/library-authoring-qualification/tools/library-contract-check.sh
#
# What it runs is the flow's own line, unchanged:
#
#   sh <workspace>/flow/analyze-library-contract.sh \
#      <workspace>/flow/library-input.json \
#      <workspace>/library-contract/library-insight.json
#
# The only thing this Pack adds around it is creating the declared output's directory: the flow writes
# its envelope with a plain open() and creates no directory of its own.
#
# Local and non-commercial. This script loads no Liberty file, invokes no QuaLib, calls no `edarun`,
# reads no production Library fact, requalifies no E1--E4 method and touches no customer data.
set -eu

: "${WORKSPACE:?the Campaign workspace on the Site}"

out="$WORKSPACE/library-contract/library-insight.json"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "$out")"

exec sh "$WORKSPACE/flow/analyze-library-contract.sh" \
  "$WORKSPACE/flow/library-input.json" \
  "$out"

args.content:
# The five fields this Pack checks, and what the reading means

This Pack checks one local, bounded input contract. Nothing here is a Liberty file, a QuaLib report, a
production Library fact or a Wave 2 E1--E4 statement, and a reading of `1 count` is not permission to
infer Library API, PVT, revision, design impact, quality or customer value.

## The input

The one handed-off input is `library-input.json`, read by the Golden Flow's own validator. Exactly one
object, with exactly these five fields:

| Field | Required shape |
| --- | --- |
| `sourceSha256` | a 64-character lower-case hexadecimal string |
| `qualification` | the literal `authoring-qualification` |
| `reportSchema` | the literal `hima-library-insight-report/1` |
| `provenance` | a non-empty string |
| `unknowns` | a non-empty list of non-empty strings |

## The envelope

The validator writes a whitelisted envelope holding only those five values, and it renames one:
the input's `reportSchema` is written as the envelope's `schema`. Both names are held against the same
literal. No other key of the input is carried forward.

Because the validator whitelists, an extra opaque success key such as `"libraryReady": true` is
ignored: it neither fails the input nor reaches the envelope, the reader or the Judge. That is a
stated limit of this local method and not a check it implements.

`qualification: authoring-qualification` is a checked field of this local contract. It is not evidence
of native QuaLib qualification, of a production Library, or of any commercial result.

## The reading

The reader emits one typed value, `library_contract_ready`, unit `count`:

- `1` — every required field was present and valid, and the envelope was read.
- no value at all — the input was absent, malformed, missing a required field, or the envelope was
  invalid. The reader exits non-zero with no value.

**There is no zero.** No reader of this Pack produces `0`, so an absent or refused reading is never
read as `0`, and the `>= 0 count` constraint has no real-zero case here. Every rule, verdict and
report must present a refusal as the absence of a value.

## What each ending means for a person

- `goal-met` — the bounded local contract was present and valid. That is the whole claim.
- `input-refused` — the input was invalid or absent. No measurement exists, and the Run is not TEST
  evidence.
- `contract-blocked` — the flow or its input could not be read on the Site. Nothing was measured.
- `budget-exhausted` — a meter ran out. It is a budget, not a verdict.

Native QuaLib qualification, production Library facts and Wave 2 E1--E4 claims are outside this
Pack's TEST.

# What this Pack's local TEST does and does not claim

## What it is

This Pack runs one local, bounded check: does the one handed-off Library authoring-qualification input
carry its declared identity, schema, qualification label, provenance and explicit unknowns, and does
the Golden Flow's own validator accept them? It exists to exercise the authoring, specification,
fabric, test and release chain against Library-method requirements. It is deliberately the smallest
thing that is still a real Campaign: one tool, one report, one reader, two ordered rules, one
decision, no loop.

## What it never does

A generation of this Pack does not load a Liberty file, invoke QuaLib, call `edarun`, use a Site EDA
wrapper, read a production Library fact, requalify the Wave 2 E1--E4 method, or touch customer data.
It holds no commercial licence seat. Its input is the flow's own local `library-input.json`, whose
`sourceSha256` field is a checked shape and not a recomputed digest.

## What a result may say

A PASS/PASS decision says only this: within this local contract, the bounded source identity was
present and was read. It is a statement about the envelope, never about a Library. A reading of
`1 count` does not establish Library API, PVT, revision, design impact, quality or customer value,
and it replaces no commercial evidence.

## Wording for a person reading an ending

- goal-met: "the local authoring-qualification contract was present and valid; no commercial Library
  claim follows from it."
- input-refused: "the input was invalid or absent, so no measurement exists; native QuaLib
  qualification, production Library facts and Wave 2 E1--E4 claims remain outside this TEST."
- contract-blocked: "the flow or its input could not be read on the Site; nothing was measured."
- budget-exhausted: "a budget was reached, which is not a verdict about the input."

A running or paused Run is not TEST evidence.

# What a Site binds, in its own site file under `bindings:`. The same Pack runs on another Site by
# editing that file, never this one.
inputs:
  - name: flowRoot
    description: >-
      The Golden Flow's root on the Site: the local authoring-qualification flow directory holding
      analyze-library-contract.sh, read-library-contract.py and library-input.json. Read-only to a
      Campaign — a generation runs in its own copy of it, never here.
  - name: workspaceRoot
    description: >-
      Where Campaign workspaces are created. The Site's Permit must allow writes under it; nothing
      this Pack does writes anywhere else.

# What a generation leaves in its Campaign workspace. Paths are relative to the workspace.
outputs:
  - name: libraryContract
    path: library-contract/library-insight.json
    reader: library-contract-reader
    description: >-
      The whitelisted envelope one generation's validator wrote — schema, qualification,
      sourceSha256, provenance and unknowns — and the judged artifact. It is read into the single
      typed value library_contract_ready. It is not a Liberty file, a QuaLib report or a production
      Library fact.

# What the Site must let this Pack run: the first word of every command line below. The Permit's
# `allowedWrappers` decides each one.
environment:
  wrappers:
    - sh
    - python3

# How a Campaign workspace is prepared from the bound flow root, once per Campaign. The copy lands in
# `<workspace>/flow/`.
workspace:
  copy:
    - analyze-library-contract.sh
    - read-library-contract.py
    - library-input.json
    - README.md

# The Pack's one tool. A person can run `tools/library-contract-check.sh` by hand and get exactly the
# command line below; no licence seat is held, because the flow needs none.
tools:
  - id: library-contract-check
    file: tools/library-contract-check.sh
    description: >-
      One generation of the Golden Flow's own validator, run inside the Campaign's own copy of the
      flow: the five-field gate over the one handed-off input. The flow's command line is unchanged;
      the only thing this Pack adds around it is creating the declared output's directory.
    inputs: [WORKSPACE]
    argv:
      - sh
      - -c
      - 'mkdir -p "$(dirname "$2")" && exec sh "$1" "$3" "$2"'
      - library-contract-check
      - ${WORKSPACE}/flow/analyze-library-contract.sh
      - ${WORKSPACE}/library-contract/library-insight.json
      - ${WORKSPACE}/flow/library-input.json

# Every rule this Pack's judge node may apply, by reference: this folder's rules/ first.
rules:
  - library-contract-nonnegative
  - library-contract-goal

# This Pack's own domain knowledge, one entry per file under knowledge/.
knowledge:
  - file: library-contract-fields.md
    purpose: >-
      the five checked fields and their required shapes, the envelope's `schema` key, and the rule
      that an absent reading is never a zero
  - file: scope-boundary.md
    purpose: >-
      what this Pack's local TEST does and does not claim, in the words a person reads beside an
      ending

# No strategy knob, declared as an empty record rather than omitted: a generation of this Pack varies
# nothing, sets nothing per generation, and the start form renders no knob for it.
strategy: {}

# The one number a Campaign binds at start. This Pack accepts exactly 1 count: the one handed-off
# input carries one identity, no knob varies it, and a different target is a new campaign.
goal:
  library_contract_target: { type: number, unit: count, min: 1, max: 1, default: 1 }

# What this Pack's number is called on the faces a person reads.
words:
  library_contract_target: { label: validated authoring-qualification contract, unit: count }

# this Pack can run, what one generation leaves in its Campaign workspace, and what the Pack runs.
# The scope is deliberately local and non-commercial. It loads no Liberty file, invokes no QuaLib,
# calls no `edarun`, reads no production Library fact, requalifies no E1--E4 method and touches no
# customer data.
id: library-authoring-qualification
version: '1'
title: Library authoring-qualification check

# What a Site binds, in its own site file under `bindings:`. The same Pack runs on another Site by
# editing that file, never this one.
inputs:
  - name: flowRoot
    description: >-
      The Golden Flow's root on the Site: the local authoring-qualification flow directory holding
      analyze-library-contract.sh, read-library-contract.py and library-input.json. Read-only to a
      Campaign — a generation runs in its own copy of it, never here.
  - name: workspaceRoot
    description: >-
      Where Campaign workspaces are created. The Site's Permit must allow writes under it; nothing
      this Pack does writes anywhere else.

# What a generation leaves in its Campaign workspace. Paths are relative to the workspace.
outputs:
  - name: libraryContract
    path: library-contract/library-insight.json
    reader: library-contract-reader
    description: >-
      The whitelisted envelope one generation's validator wrote — schema, qualification,
      sourceSha256, provenance and unknowns — and the judged artifact. It is read into the single
      typed value library_contract_ready. It is not a Liberty file, a QuaLib report or a production
      Library fact.

# What the Site must let this Pack run: the first word of every command line below. The Permit's
# `allowedWrappers` decides each one.
environment:
  wrappers:
    - sh
    - python3

# How a Campaign workspace is prepared from the bound flow root, once per Campaign. The copy lands in
# `<workspace>/flow/`.
workspace:
  copy:
    - analyze-library-contract.sh
    - read-library-contract.py
    - library-input.json
    - README.md

# The Pack's one tool. A person can run `tools/library-contract-check.sh` by hand and get exactly the
# command line below; no licence seat is held, because the flow needs none.
tools:
  - id: library-contract-check
    file: tools/library-contract-check.sh
    description: >-
      One generation of the Golden Flow's own validator, run inside the Campaign's own copy of the
      flow: the five-field gate over the one handed-off input. The flow's command line is unchanged;
      the only thing this Pack adds around it is creating the declared output's directory.
    inputs: [WORKSPACE]
    argv:
      - sh
      - -c
      - 'mkdir -p "$(dirname "$2")" && exec sh "$1" "$3" "$2"'
      - library-contract-check
      - ${WORKSPACE}/flow/analyze-library-contract.sh
      - ${WORKSPACE}/library-contract/library-insight.json
      - ${WORKSPACE}/flow/library-input.json

# Every rule this Pack's judge node may apply, by reference: this folder's rules/ first.
rules:
  - library-contract-nonnegative
  - library-contract-goal

# This Pack's own domain knowledge, one entry per file under knowledge/.
knowledge:
  - file: library-contract-fields.md
    purpose: >-
      the five checked fields and their required shapes, the envelope's `schema` key, and the rule
      that an absent reading is never a zero
  - file: scope-boundary.md
    purpose: >-
      what this Pack's local TEST does and does not claim, in the words a person reads beside an
      ending

# No strategy knob, declared as an empty record rather than omitted: a generation of this Pack varies
# nothing, sets nothing per generation, and the start form renders no knob for it.
strategy:
  diagnosticProbe: { type: number, unit: count, min: 1, max: 1, default: 1 }

# The one number a Campaign binds at start. This Pack accepts exactly 1 count: the one handed-off
# input carries one identity, no knob varies it, and a different target is a new campaign.
goal:
  library_contract_target: { type: number, unit: count, min: 1, max: 1, default: 1 }

# What this Pack's number is called on the faces a person reads.
words:
  library_contract_target: { label: validated authoring-qualification contract, unit: count }
  diagnosticProbe: { label: temporary diagnostic stand-in, unit: count }

## Files written

- contract.yml — the run contract: two Site bindings, two wrappers-worth of declared command lines
  (`sh`), the `libraryContract` output and its reader, the workspace copy of four flow files, one
  tool, two rules, two knowledge files, an empty Strategy and the one goal parameter.
- graph.yml — five nodes (`check-contract`, `read-contract`, `judge`, `decide`, `blocked`), four
  edges and no revisit: the acts, the two ordered rules, the one Explore decision and the wait node.
- semantics.yml — the one value type this Pack's own reader emits, `library_contract_ready`, unit
  `count`.
- rules/library-contract-nonnegative.yml — the constraint rule, `library_contract_ready >= 0 count`.
- rules/library-contract-goal.yml — the goal rule, `library_contract_ready >= library_contract_target`.
- choosers/library-contract-decide.yml — the one Explore clause: `constraint: PASS, goal: PASS` →
  `goalMet: true`.
- readers/library-contract-reader.yml — the declaration over the flow's own reader: argv
  `sh ${READER} ${REPORT} ${OUT}`, emitting `library_contract_ready`.
- tools/library-contract-check.sh — the Pack-local script holding the tool's declared command line:
  the flow's own `analyze-library-contract.sh` over `library-input.json`, inside the Campaign's flow
  copy, plus the `mkdir` for the declared output directory.
- tools/read-library-contract.sh — the Pack-local reader script: the flow's own
  `read-library-contract.py`, run from the Campaign's flow copy, writing the reading document or
  exiting non-zero with no value.
- knowledge/library-contract-fields.md — the five checked fields, the envelope's `schema` key, the
  no-zero rule, and what each ending means for a person.
- knowledge/scope-boundary.md — what this Pack's local TEST does and does not claim, in the words a
  person reads beside an ending.
- FABRIC.md — this record.

## Gaps

- `strategy` — the spec's approved method declares no knob (`Run contract`: "**Strategy.** None. No
  knob of this Pack is set for a generation … nothing between generations varies"; `Choosers`: "It
  sets no strategy knob, because this Pack has none"), and this harness refuses a contract whose
  Strategy is empty beside an Explore node:
  `strategy: declares no knob, and a pack whose Strategy has nothing in it has nothing for an Explore
  node to choose`. Nothing in the Golden Flow offers one: both its commands take only an input path
  and an output path. What the author has to decide: approve one fixed, non-varying strategy knob by
  amending `SPEC.md` through `/hima-spec`, or keep the source-approved no-knob method and accept that
  the folder stops at `specified` and cannot host a Campaign on this harness.
- `environment.wrappers` — the spec's `Run contract` names `sh` and `python3`, and this folder holds
  only `sh`: no command line this Pack declares starts with `python3`, because the reader's declared
  first word is `sh` and the flow's own `read-library-contract.py` runs inside it, and the harness
  refuses a declared wrapper that no declared command line uses
  (`contract.yml: environment.wrappers declares "python3", which no tool, workshop or reader of this
  pack runs`). The capability is still required on the Site and nothing in this folder can declare
  it: the Golden Flow's validator and reader both run `python3` internally, so a Site whose Permit
  forbids it cannot host this Pack.

No gap of the first kind exists: every tool and reader the contract names is in this folder, and
`hima_pack_check` resolves both rules, the reader, the chooser, the semantics entry and both knowledge
files.

  tools/library-contract-check.sh: runs the Golden Flow's own `analyze-library-contract.sh` over

  tools/read-library-contract.sh: runs the Golden Flow's own `read-library-contract.py` from the
